name: Jonah
overview: Jonah was a male prophet, the son of Amittai, originating from Gath-hepher, as noted in 2 Kings 14:25. He is uniquely identified by his prophetic calling and his significant ministry recorded in Scripture. No additional tribal or familial details are provided beyond his father and hometown.
namesAndTitles: The name Jonah means 'dove,' reflecting a proper name given in Hebrew context as recorded in 2 Kings 14:25. This single name does not have an explicitly divine origin but carries symbolic resonance within the biblical narrative.
familyAndRelationships: Jonah is explicitly identified as the son of Amittai according to 2 Kings 14:25. Beyond this paternal relationship, Scripture does not record any other family connections for Jonah.
scriptureSignificance: Jonah's prophetic mission highlights God's sovereign call and mercy, especially toward Gentile nations like Nineveh. His initial reluctance and subsequent obedience demonstrate the tension between divine compassion and human response. Jonah's experience of being swallowed by a great fish for three days serves as a powerful foreshadowing of Christ's death and resurrection, emphasizing God's redemptive plan for all peoples.
